sent.text: Fair warning: selling an elephant is not a quick business.
Elephants take their time.
So does this video: almost eight minutes.
Yes, eight.
Grab a coffee.
Maybe two.
You can't rush an elephant.
Believe us, we tried.
We promise the elephant is worth it.
Maybe websites aren't mandatory where you are.
They will matter anyway.
A website is the only channel a school fully controls.
Search engines read it.
AI answers are built from it.
Agents will act on it.
What matters is not how it looks, but whether it's current.
We often hear: you're offering a template.
The alternative is a unique design.
But nothing is entirely unique, and a design starts to age from day one.
In the mock-up, made-up content looks great.
Real content is added by the school itself.
One colleague prepared a text, another pasted it as it came.
The head got an email and asked to change the menu.
Parents missed a document, so it was moved “higher”.
Nobody means any harm.
The website simply becomes everyone's, and no one's.
That's how the twelve mistakes that catch the eye the most are born.
Each mistake looks like a detail.
Together, they make a good school look worse than it is.
Now multiply it by a hundred schools.
Five hundred… and more.
Schools learn from each other.
Sadly, mistakes travel that way too.
The same mistakes, thousands of times.
That's how the whole system looks.
Let's address the elephant in the room.
Every school has the same duties: accessibility, data protection, security, and rules that keep changing.
Most face them alone, with their own budget and their own contractor.
So quality comes down to chance.
And every few years: a new tender, a new website.
The tree is cut back to a stump and planted again.
And again.
Each time, continuity is lost.
Ours is never cut down.
Wind bent it, rain soaked it, seasons changed it: new rules, new technology, visitors who expect more every year.
It only grew stronger.
And now nobody argues that it was worth it.
Cleverphant is shared digital infrastructure for schools.
What people see is the website.
Underneath is everything that keeps it right, from one design system to compliance and support, shared by every school.
A new school simply plugs in.
What is a design system?
A set of ready-made parts.
Colours, fonts and buttons make blocks: a search field, a staff card.
Blocks make sections, sections make pages.
Every page of every school is built from the same parts, and every part already meets accessibility rules: contrast, headings, keyboard.
Improve one part once, and it improves everywhere.
Some see us as an agency.
Others, as yet another do-it-yourself website builder.
We are neither: we are a platform with a human touch.
Nobody starts from a blank page: we move the old website for the school, its pages, documents and staff profiles, cleaned up on the way.
We ask the school a few clarifying questions and to fill in what is missing.
Not much work, but the school's part matters.
The school checks, and the new website goes live.
Because every school runs on the same system, they all get the same benefits.
And yes.
the same bugs.
It happens.
But it takes just one school to notice.
Fixed once, fixed for all.
The same goes for knowledge.
When one school asks a question, the answer becomes a lesson, a video and a newsletter for every school.
Ideas travel the same way.
An innovative school leader brings a need.
Their school becomes the pilot.
The pilot runs in a loop: need, analysis and design, build, testing, evaluation, and round again.
Slow.
Very slow.
Then the data shows it works, and every school has it at once.
Schools learn from each other anyway.
Here, they adopt what has been tested.
And it can work from the top, too.
What is common to every school is updated once: accessibility, update subscriptions, cookies.
It appears on every school website at the same time.
No emails.
No reminders.
None left out.
Distribution is already solved.
So a big network can afford big ideas: things no single school could ever build alone, built once and shared by all.
A small village school gets what a large city school gets.
One design system underneath; the face stays the school's own.
Not a template: a model on working infrastructure, with your content.
Not identical.
Equally good.
Change starts with details.
Being small is no excuse to look away.
Elephants are slow.
Very slow.
So slow that nobody notices the change, until it's everywhere.
That's our Trojan elephant.
It is also the biggest job: hundreds of school websites have to stay accessible, current and stable.
How do you eat an elephant like that?
One bite at a time, continuously.
Small improvements, cosmetic fixes and bug fixes ship regularly and consistently, to all schools.
That is our strength: the bigger the network, the more eyes notice, and the more schools gain from every improvement and every extra touch.
And every next step lands on every school: live tables, whistleblower channels, consultation booking, individual education plan forms, event calendars, weekly update digests.
And we keep asking: what if?
What if a teacher's Word file became a finished article?
What if documents named and filed themselves?
What if a fix was ready before you saw the problem?
None of this needs a new website.
Each idea is an app on the same foundation.
One school pilots it, every school gets it.
And AI?
Not another chatbot.
AI that quietly keeps things in order.
Because AI loves order.
What works in one school works in a municipality, a region, a whole country.
Schools can be added quickly, while costs grow far more slowly.
Not a promise of cheap.
The logic of scale.
We have walked this road for fifteen years.
The first ten?
Slow.
Very slow.
So slow.
Change in schools takes time.
Then the network started to grow by itself.
Today: almost three hundred institutions on one standard, with at least one client in eighty-five percent of Lithuania's municipalities.
You don't have to start from the slow part.
Audits, onboarding and training are ready.
And an elephant never forgets: when staff change, the knowledge stays.
The goal was never the websites.
It is giving teachers back to their students.
Built in a small country.
Ready for yours.
Across the European Union, public institutions share the same rules: web accessibility, data protection, whistleblower protection.
Built for one, ready for all.
Let's talk about your region.
